text: # Dispatch brief

Every brief carries: claims as pasted command output (source, n, denominator) or `UNVERIFIED — check before relying on it`, absences and external facts too; every signature, exit code, path or flag it cites is copied from a grep run in this turn, with file:line; a state line is pasted `git log -1 --format=%h; git status --porcelain` output, never typed; a file list for a changed symbol is pasted `command grep -rln <symbol> scripts/ src/ tests/` output; the implementer runs its importing tests first.

A re-derivation that contradicts a seat lists every category the number ranges over with its contribution (UNRESOLVED/UNKNOWN as their own row); a commit saying a seat overstated waits for a second seat to re-derive it.

Also: files the agent owns and must not touch, the environment block from the agent file, the job-spec handoff (it never waits on SGE), and the closing line *"report anything in this brief that you found to be wrong."* Review briefs add the template below: findings file created first and written by the seat itself with its own Write/heredoc (a missing file, or one without `## CLOSING`, means re-run the seat; controller transcription is the last resort and is marked) (findings dir, never scratchpad; scripts you write for evidence go in `<findings dir>/probes/<seat>/`, never the scratchpad; no other writes, nothing under the project tree, its `.claude/agent-memory/` included:

R-20261110-2, a seat's memory write nearly failed a running build's tree guard), at most 4 ranked areas with a drop order, `git log -1 --format=%h` re-run before each finding's evidence line (cited file changed: mark it `RE-DERIVE`; the controller edits no file a running seat reads), the minor-triage question, and the unenumerated-objection slot.
An analysis brief opens with a TARGET sentence and what a result would have to show to answer it; the domain seat checks the headline against it.
A review that closes a register row re-measures the row's premise against the real source (live call, fixture vs claim), not only the diff.
A multi-seat brief names one owner (file or seat) per shared fact (a count, a register row); other seats cite it rather than re-derive it.
**Which seat.** Code tasks (SDD included) go to `implementer` on its default sonnet;
`model: opus` only for a cross-module or contract change or a retry, with that reason in the brief's first line (DECISION-028).
Ad hoc questions go to `investigator`; "where is X" to Explore with `model: haiku`.
Never general-purpose.
The implementer runs only its own tests and the linter, and stops instead of asking: this overrides the SDD template.
Name the project and paste the path of its domain-context file(s); seats omit CLAUDE.md.
At most 2 subagents at once (3 on the larger account); queue the rest.
Every implementer brief also carries:

*"Lean checks before commit: no pass-through wrappers, no assert, gate, control arm or oracle that cannot fail: each ships a fail proof (one input that changes only the field it reads, where it differs from the passing value, reaching the failing verdict; both values pasted) or is labelled 'cannot fail' and never prints PASS/ok; an oracle lists the inputs it shares with the code; a docstring naming a published rule has a toy test where rule and variant differ, or says 'variant of'; no test that re-implements the code under test, and each error message says what the check does."* Review seats other than research-scout can write their findings file with a Bash heredoc; a seat that answers only in its message has not followed its brief.

**Turn budget, first line of every implementer brief:** *"Commit your finished work and write your report by turn 70 of 100; leave the rest as a listed remainder."* A task that still hits 100 is too big: split it.

**DONE line:** the exact test command and its pass count; for a changed return contract or cache producer, the pasted callers grep and the digest/namespace bumped; the project's governance tests (its CLAUDE.md or CI list) run; the report written to `<findings dir>/<task>-implementer.md` before the reply, so a restart does not lose it; a `RESULT:` line per headline number, unrounded (3 significant figures) with its n, which the controller quotes verbatim and recounts from the artifact before writing it into a doc.
A plan box is ticked only against the promise's quoted wording, else `partial: <what is missing>`.
Before each implementer dispatch, re-read the session's done-condition and the wave's Goal line.
Every review brief ends with:
*"Append each finding to your findings file as you find it; the file is your report.
Before your last turn, append `## CLOSING`: objection, errors in this brief, what you did not cover.
Your final message is at most 10 lines: verdict, counts, the file path."*
